**US (Rule 6c-11):** The rule sets conditions for ETFs to operate without individual exemptive relief, including custom-basket policies and daily disclosure. It doesn't prescribe AP agreement parties. In practice, the AP agreement is typically signed by the issuing trust (usually a Delaware statutory trust) on behalf of a specific fund series, with the principal underwriter/distributor and the authorized participant (a broker-dealer and DTC participant) as counterparties. The trust has no separate legal personality, so the signature block and series designation matter.

**Ireland (ICAV):** An ICAV is a corporate vehicle with separate legal personality under the ICAV Act 2015, governed by a board and Central Bank of Ireland UCITS rules. Its umbrella structure gives statutory segregation between sub-funds. Participating dealers sign agreements with the ICAV and its distributor, and a UCITS depositary plays an oversight role with no direct US equivalent. Rule 6c-11 has no Irish analogue.
